name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
summary_text: Bosnia and Herzegovina is workable for trans visitors. Nothing is criminalised; Sarajevo Pride has proceeded annually since 2019 with heavy (necessary) police protection; and most cantons have now appointed prosecutors specifically for anti-LGBTI hate crimes — genuine institutional progress. Counterweights from the 2024 Pink Report: negative events are accumulating, the trend is unfavourable outside Sarajevo (especially Republika Srpska), and trans people occupy a “precarious position” — no legal gender recognition framework, restricted healthcare access, and institutional suspicion. The state is also deeply dysfunctional generally. For a visitor: no legal exposure; stick to Sarajevo and tourist areas; avoid visible trans presentation in Republika Srpska and rural areas.

sources.title: Pink Report 2024 – Annual Report on the State of the Human Rights of LGBT Persons in Bosnia and Herzegovina – Sarajevski Otvoreni Centar
sources.claim_summary: Sarajevo Open Centre's Pink Report 2024 (annual report on the human rights of LGBT persons in Bosnia and Herzegovina): the position of LGBTI people is unsatisfactory nationwide with a growing disparity between the two entities. In Republika Srpska there was an organised hooligan attack on BH Pride March activists in Banja Luka, incitement to violence and discrimination by the entity's highest officials, and organised anti-LGBT groups.

sources.title: The Precarious Position of Trans Bodies in Bosnia and Herzegovina | Balkan Diskurs
sources.claim_summary: Balkan Diskurs feature (Oct 2024): legal gender recognition is formally accessible across BiH but described as vague and ineffective in practice - legal texts imply it requires complete medical transition, contradicting self-determination (criticised by the European Parliament). Without documents matching appearance, trans people face difficulties accessing housing and jobs; medical transition becomes a prerequisite for basic rights.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023) chapter on BiH: eight SOGIESC hate-speech cases documented ahead of Sarajevo Pride; prosecutor offices in the majority of cantons now have staff overseeing anti-LGBTI hate crimes; the Federal Government instructed the Justice Ministry to draft a same-sex partnership law; the first Constitutional Court appeal was filed over non-recognition of a Croatian-issued same-sex partnership; extremists roamed Banja Luka chanting 'kill the...' before Pride events.

sources.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina: Attack on LGBT Activists | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Feb 2014): 'Bosnia and Herzegovina: Attack on LGBT Activists' — condemns a violent attack on Sarajevo Pride organisers; impunity and hate-motive failures documented.

sources.title: Gay Life in Bosnia and Herzegovina
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz report (2012): 'Gay Life in Bosnia and Herzegovina' - decriminalised in FBiH (1996) and RS (1998); the 2009 anti-discrimination law covers sexual orientation/sexual expression but omitted gender identity; describes a homophobic society across the two entities.

sources.title: Better protection of LGBTI persons through the amendments to the Anti-discrimination Law of BiH – Sarajevski Otvoreni Centar
sources.claim_summary: Sarajevo Open Centre (July 2016): BiH's amended Anti-discrimination Law explicitly covers sexual orientation and gender identity (with correct local terminology) and 'sex characteristics' - the first country in South-East Europe to protect intersex people in all spheres; also improves harassment definitions and procedures.

sources.title: Federation of BiH finally adopts hate crime regulation – Sarajevski Otvoreni Centar
sources.claim_summary: Sarajevo Open Centre (July 2016): the Federation of BiH adopted hate-crime regulation covering sexual orientation and gender identity as aggravating circumstances - all three BiH administrative units now regulate hate crimes in their criminal codes.
